entries.name: nyiso_gas_commitment_bridge (min_load_frac + min_run_hours)
entries.source: ALL FOUR values read from ONE frozen derive artifact, data/raw/_processed-legacy/campd_gas_commitment_params_NYISO.csv (scripts/data/derive_campd_gas_commitment_params.py, EPA CAMPD unit-level hourly grossLoad 2023-2025, 78 units). min_load_frac = the capacity-weighted p50 across units of each unit's own LSL/HSL ratio, where HSL = p99.5 of pooled load and LSL = p5 of online-hour load (the WP-3 loading-when-on construction + the derive_cc_committed_pct.py p5-of-online minimum-stable statistic). min_run_hours = the capacity-weighted p50 of the measured run-length distribution (CC p25/p50/p75 = 11/21/133 h; ST_GAS 3/13/89 h). NYISO publishes no 60-Day-DAM equivalent of the ERCOT LSL/HSL disclosure, which is why the ratio is reconstructed from the meter; the reconstructed CC value 0.523 lands within 9 % of ERCOT's independently PUBLISHED cap-weighted p50 of 0.574 — an outside cross-check that the construction is not self-referential.
entries.note: ZERO residual identification: no value was chosen for its effect on a price or volume residual, and none was swept. The capacity weighting is forced by what the parameter does (a min-run constraint floors committed MW, not committed unit-count) and is the same weighting min_load_frac uses. The min-run values DISAGREE with the published class tables in OPPOSITE directions — CC 21 h is an increase over the table's 5-10 h, ST_GAS 13 h a decrease from its 24-48 h — which is itself evidence the values follow the measurement rather than a residual: a residual-fitted pair would not move against a published table in one class and with it in the other. Caveat recorded: an OBSERVED run length is an upper-ish bound on a minimum-run CONSTRAINT, so the low percentiles bound it from the side the constraint lives on; the p50 is the deliberate, documented choice and re-derives ONLY when the CAMPD vintages update (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]). The mechanism's other inputs add no parameters at all: min-down and startup cost come from the published NREL/SR-5500-55433 class tables the model already used, the DA horizon is the tariff-cited DA_COMMITMENT_HORIZON_HOURS=24, and the restart inequality is priced at the model's OWN P0 duals. n_residual UNCHANGED at 6.

construction.gross_to_net: divided by the COMMITTED parasitic factor (parasitic_load_factors.parquet) -- the same map run_calibration_full._campd_hourly_frame uses to build the benchmark's net actual
construction.plant_aggregation: generation-weighted mean over the plant's turbines

entries.source: EPA CAMPD unit-level hourly grossLoad + heatInput. Replaces the eGRID PLANT-AVERAGE ANNUAL heat rate, which is neither a loaded rate nor -- at a mixed facility -- the right technology's rate (E F Barrett 2511: 1971 FT4 turbines and 188 MW steam boilers share one 11.076; measured separately the turbines run 16.69. Bayswater 55699 carries a non-physical 21.68 against a measured 10.74).
entries.identification_note: ZERO fitted scalars. Every value is a measured unit-conduct statistic; no parameter of the construction (window, percentile, minimum hours, band) was chosen by looking at a residual. Rule 13 [R-MEASURED] admissible: a machine's loaded heat rate regenerates for a forward year from the same pipeline and responds to changed conditions (a retrofit moves it; a new unit carries its design rate). Rule 24 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]: re-derives ONLY on a CAMPD vintage change.
entries.root_cause: OPEN (LOYO caveat, nyiso-89): re-deriving the artifact leaving each year out is stable for 16 of 19 plants (<5 % spread) and never reverses the correction's sign on any plant that carries its weight -- Bayonne 0.5 %, Bayswater 1.0 %, Port Jefferson 2.8 %, Barrett 6.1 % (16.07-17.09, never approaching the eGRID 11.08). It is NOT stable on the two low-utilization 1970s barge plants: Gowanus 2494 (16.5 % spread) and Narrows 2499 (12.8 %), where dropping 2025 reverses the sign vs eGRID. Those plants are thin-sampled (0.09 and 0.22 TWh of measured energy across three years) and sit far out of merit at EVERY fold value (13.2-16.2 MMBtu/MWh against a class base near 10), so no gate moves. A minimum-energy screen for thin-sampled plants is the named follow-up; it is deliberately NOT added here, because adding a screen after seeing the LOYO result would be a post-hoc choice (rule 24).

entries.lineage_solves: 0 solves added to the tuning lineage — the mechanism was built to a pre-registration (docs/handoffs/nyiso96-preregistration.md, committed before the A/B launched) and A/B-tested ONCE against its same-HEAD zero-delta control (2026-07-29-nyiso-96-control-zerodelta). entries.value: Each thermal tranche's offer adds start_cost_per_mw / expected_run_hours: start costs from the NREL BIN_STARTUP_COST_PER_MW table already ledgered for the committed tranche ($20/MW CT_PEAKER/CT_CHP, $50/MW CC duct bands); expected run hours from the plant's own measured CAMPD run-length p50 (campd_ct_run_lengths_NYISO.csv, 22 plants + pooled class fallback 4.0 h, 34,057 measured runs 2023-2025). Realised offer increment ~$5/MWh on the CT bands, as pre-registered.
entries.source: NREL startup-cost table (docs/parameter-citations.md, pre-existing citation) + data/raw CAMPD unit conduct reduced by the frozen derive scripts/data/derive_campd_ct_run_lengths.py (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]: re-derives only on a CAMPD source update). No parameter is ported from another ISO (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]) and none is fitted to a residual.
entries.forward_story: Both inputs regenerate for a forward year: the NREL table is a published engineering constant, and the run-length basis re-derives from rolling CAMPD history conditioned on the fleet, responding to changed conditions through the runs the fleet actually produces (rule 13 admissibility).
entries.rule_13_admissibility: A start-cost amortization over a measured expected run length is a market-design input (bid production cost recovery), not an outcome pinned to a residual: no volume or price is pinned, the LP still chooses dispatch, and prices remain LP duals (rule 4 [R-DUALS]).
